_readme: Chain-agnostic conformance corpus extracted one-for-one from the reference Soroban test suite (contract-level tests only). Schema: spec/07-scenarios.md; vocabulary: spec/01..05. One scenario per reference test, in source order; `source` = <file>::<mod path>::<fn>.

MACROS. `{"step":"seed","on":C,"data_id":D,"as":S,"n":N}` expands, for k in 1..=N, to `{"step":"advance","to":100+k}` followed by a `call on_report` as S with the default metadata (owner:0x11, name:0x22, cid zero32, report_id 0x0000) and entries `[{data_id:D, answer:k*100, timestamp:k*10}]`, expected ok. It is the reference harness's `seed(feed, n)`; the `macros` object below restates it.

ADDITIONS TO 07 (each is a test-only convention, listed so the schema can absorb them): (1) `advance` also accepts `{"to": n}` = set the sequence to absolute ledger n (the reference rolls to absolute numbers; every `to` is monotone within a scenario; the environment starts at sequence 0). (2) `{"step":"age_ttl"}` = advance to half the network maximum TTL so every refreshable lifetime is measurably below the maximum; requires `expiry`. (3) `expect_ttl.is` also accepts `"below_max"` (the reference's sanity check that aging actually lowered the lifetime). (4) `expect_ttl` keys: `record` is `instance` (contract instance), or `FeedConfig`/`FeedState`/`MinDecimals` with `data_id`, `FeedAdmin` with `admin`, `Permission` with `data_id`+`sender`+`owner`+`name`. (5) `expect_events.ordered: true` = the listed events must appear in that relative order among the call's events. (6) `deploy` also accepts `what: mock_cache | mock_cache2` (bound to the names `cache`/`cache2`) — a Cache double with injectable state, used by every proxy unit test; and `{"step":"mock_cache","on":"cache"|"cache2","data_id":D,"rounds":[Round...],"latest":Round,"frozen":bool,"fail_with":code}` sets its state (only the fields given change). The double answers `decimals([..])` with 18 and `description([..])` with "MOCK" for any id, `latest_round`/`get_round` from `latest`/`rounds` (null when unset), `is_frozen` from `frozen` (false when unset); once `fail_with` is set every `latest_round`/`get_round`/`decimals`/`description` call returns that Cache error code (`is_frozen` still answers). `rounds`/`latest` carry `round_id`, `answer`, `timestamp` (ledger_seq 1000, primary true in the reference; not observable through the Proxy). (7) `{"step":"expect_balance","token":"token","of":ACTOR,"is":n}` reads the token balance of an actor. (8) `{"step":"expect_error_codes","contract":C,"codes":{Name:code},"range":[lo,hi],"ownership_range":[lo,hi]}` = static assertion that every named error has that numeric code, all lie within `range`, none collides with the ownership library's codes, and the ownership library's codes lie within `ownership_range` (the reference checks its three OwnableError codes). (9) `call.expect` also accepts `{"decode_fail": true}` = the platform decoder's failure for undecodable report bytes (Soroban: `Error(Value, InvalidInput)` trap; see the overlay). (10) `on_report` takes `args: {sender, report}` where `report` is the schema's report value; the harness splits it into the `metadata` and `report` byte arguments. `report.trailing_bytes` (hex) is appended after the canonical serialisation of `entries`; `raw_metadata`/`raw_report` replace the encoded form verbatim. (11) `expire_round` carries `on`.

VALUE MATCHING in `expect.value`: an object asserts only the fields it lists (partial match); a list asserts length and each element positionally; `null` asserts absence/None; `"_"` matches anything at that position; `"some"` matches any non-null value. Addresses are actor names or contract names (`cache`, `cache2`, `proxy`). Answers are decimal strings. `bound` is `AtOrBefore`|`AtOrAfter`. Permissions in values/events/entries are `{sender, owner, name}` (the spec's `allowed_sender`, `allowed_workflow_owner`, `allowed_workflow_name`).

ACTORS: `owner` is the constructor owner everywhere. Every reference `add_admin()`/`new_address()` is bound to `admin`/`admin2`, `sender`/`sender2`, `stranger` (any address that must not be recognised: non-admin caller, unknown sender, attacker), `new_owner`, and `payer` (the token-recovery destination). `as` is always given for mutators; it is the address that must authorise on per_arg_auth platforms and the transaction signer elsewhere. `"as":"unauthorised"` appears once (cache.on_report.sender_without_auth_host_fails, requires per_arg_auth).

EVENTS: Soroban's `events().all()` holds only the last invocation's events, so every `expect_events` refers to the immediately preceding `call`. `only: true` = exactly the listed events; `count: n` = the call emitted n events. Where the reference used `assert_latest_event` on a call that emits exactly one event it is written as `only: true`; where it only counted events the names are still listed (`FeedUpdated` x2) because the assertion message names them.

DEVIATIONS: (a) The three set_feed_configs resurrection scenarios (stale_feed_state_resurrects..., re_add_by_a_different_workflow..., re_add_first_report_is_rejected_stale...) omit the reference's incidental `set_network_max_ttl(1_000_000)`: no assertion in those tests depends on it (rounds are written at ledger 1000 and nothing rolls past their lifetime under any default), and keeping it would tag core resurrection behaviour with `network_max_variable` and make it inapplicable on chains that cannot vary the network maximum. The `roll(1_000)` is kept as `advance to 1000`. (b) Duplicate identical assertions in the reference (e.g. `is_frozen` asserted twice in a row) are written once. (c) Where the reference captured values before an upgrade and compared after, the corpus spells out the known values (the seed is deterministic), so the post-upgrade steps assert every field of every round explicitly. (d) `cache.on_report.i256_answer_beyond_i128_survives` drops the reference's `to_i128().is_none()` check; it is implied by the exact 2^255-1 answer.
UNTRANSLATED: none. All 117 cache and 62 proxy contract-level tests are present (117 + 62 = 179 scenarios).
